summary: evt-dispatcher ships a staged native dropper that executes an encrypted sidecar on require()
details: The package is published as an event emitter but ships two platform-specific native addons (native.napi.node for Linux, native_win.node for Windows) that index.js unconditionally loads on require. The addons read an undeclared 1.3MB high-entropy sidecar file `.napi_cache` at the package root (not listed in package.json), stage it to a temporary path (`/tmp/.<pid>` on Linux, `%TEMP%\*.nc<id>.js` on Windows), set executable permissions, and spawn a detached child process to execute it — on Linux via fork+setsid+execlp, on Windows via CreateProcessA invoking `node "%s"` on the staged file with hidden file attributes. Before detonating, the loaders enumerate CI and sandbox indicators (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, SANDBOX), parse `/proc/1/cgroup`, `/proc/1/cmdline`, and `/proc/self/status` (TracerPid) for container/debugger traces, call IsDebuggerPresent/CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, and iterate processes for wireshark/httpdebug, gating execution to run only outside analysis environments. An event-dispatcher library has no legitimate need for native code, an encrypted sidecar, or anti-analysis gating; the native addon is a loader/decryptor and `.napi_cache` is the next-stage payload, producing arbitrary code execution on the installer's host upon any import of the module.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
